- First release: animated 2D avatars for characters and personas in Roleplay and Game.
- Works with PNGTuber-style sprites (your own expression sprites, with blink and talk pictures) and mesh avatar files.
- Ships the prompts for making blink and talk pictures and a mesh avatar from one of your sprites.

- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.
- Clicking elsewhere in the chat no longer closes Beholder when you opened it from its shortcut. It stays open until you close it or leave the chat.
- Closing the first-open note, or picking from the build menu, no longer closes Beholder when you opened it from its shortcut.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.
- Paper-doll slots can be reached by keyboard and opened with Enter or Space. Their focus outline stays visible, and closing the editor returns focus to its slot.

- The Bulk Card Editor's draft now keeps every character you added, including ones found by search, with their notes and styles. Removing a card or changing its style saves too.
- An **Unsent draft** entry at the top of the run list reopens it, and Setup says how many characters and notes came back.
- **Rerun selected** in a run's bar opens Setup with just the checked cards, their notes and styles, and the old run's settings. Adjust and start; the old run stays in History.
- Setup errors, such as a card that cannot be loaded, now show in the run summary under the settings. They used to land in a column to the right, off screen.

- The bulk Card Editor is one workspace now, laid over the character editor (a full sheet on phones). A run rail on the left, a stage bar (Setup, Processing, Review, Finish) on top.
- Setup shows targets, settings and a run summary side by side. **New run** works without a library selection: search to add characters. The schema editor opens in place.
- A run lists every card with status filters and name search. Pick a card to see it in the inspector: Changes, Split, Prompt & retry, Raw output or Details. No more stacked dialogs.
- Check cards to approve or reject them together. Approve all, rerun failed, duplicate, combine, Avatar studio and delete sit in one bar.

- **Approve all** and the automatic save after a run no longer write the same card twice. Both could pick up one planned save at the same moment, which left extra copies in duplicate mode and made cards flicker between "awaiting review" and "approved".
- The style character picker lists each card's title and first tags, and says when a search is not valid character query syntax.

- The Bulk Card Editor no longer closes when you click outside it, and it auto-saves as you type: settings and per-card notes come back the next time it opens, with **Start fresh** to discard them. A dispatch clears the draft.
- New **Presets** section: save every setting under a name, then load, overwrite or delete it later.

- Declares the Engine fork's own capability track (fork capability API 10.0) for its selection action, agent panel, overlay and structured output, and upstream capability API 1.66. Upstream Engines now refuse it instead of installing a package they cannot run. Needs an Engine fork build with fork capability API 10.0.
- The selection bar button shows only its icon when the Engine names it in a tooltip (hover or long touch), matching the other bulk actions.

- New **Transform to a schema** task: rebuild cards into Simple, Complex or your own schemas (new **Schema studio**) and write them as Markdown, XML or JSON. The model answers with structured fields by default; the old "write the document" method stays as an option.
- A card that describes several characters can stay on one card or **split**. Every split asks first (accept, rename, retry as one card, skip); split characters become new linked cards and the source card is never changed. Batches handle splits too.
- Optional **Phase 2** refines every Phase 1 result before anything is written.
- **Avatar studio** composites the run's card images into one avatar.
- Uses provider **structured output** when the agent switch is on and the connection supports it (Engine Capability API 1.342+).
- The workspace now fills most of the screen and shows run totals and split lineage.
- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.

- Responses with near-miss JSON (trailing commas, output cut off before its closing brackets) are now **auto-healed** before the strict-JSON retry, so fewer cards end in failed-parse.
- Cards that still fail to parse open a **Fix JSON** dialog with the raw model response: edit and apply it without a new model call, retry generation, or dismiss. Failed-parse rows keep a Fix JSON action to reopen it.

- Duplicate save mode gains **four independent name affixes** in the dispatch dialog: append prefix and append suffix now both apply together (the old "prefix wins over suffix" rule is gone), and the new **remove prefix** / **remove suffix** boxes strip matching text from the copy's name — case-insensitively, once each — before the append affixes wrap it. Blank boxes are simply omitted.
- The suffix box comes pre-filled with the **" (Edited)"** suggestion (remembered configs override it; clearing it means no suffix), and the chat entry's prefix remains just an editable suggestion in the prefix box.
- A live **Copy name** preview under the affix fields shows the resulting name, computed from the first target's card exactly the way the copy will be renamed.

- The bulk dispatch dialog now supports **Combined — create one new card**: each character's generated XML document is joined into a single new card's description (no per-card writes), with a required combined card name.
- Duplicate dispatches gain an optional **name prefix** that replaces the default " (Edited)" suffix, matching the engine's unified process flow.
- The auto-approve save mode is relabeled to make clear it saves each character's latest revision, and it is disabled with a visible hint whenever the bulk settings require review.
- The overlay dispatch accepts a **prefill** payload (preset, instruction, save mode, prefix, combined name, label) — the engine's "Process characters with Card Editor" entry opens this dialog fully configured, and every prefilled field stays editable.

- Dispatches that omit a concurrency value now follow the panel's bulk settings (`maxParallelAgents`, default 4) instead of running serially — RP Chat "Process cards" runs parallelize like panel dispatches, while explicit values stay untouched.
- The bulk dispatch dialog starts the parallel-agents field at the effective cap (connection limit ∩ panel cap) when no previous value is remembered; remembered values still only clamp down.
- Review previews now decode HTML entities in diff lines, full-field views, and word-count chips, matching the already-decoded applied text.

- New **Bulk settings** panel on the Runs page: cap how many agents a bulk run may drive at once (0 = follow the connection's limit, otherwise 1–16), and a **require review** toggle that disables auto-approve and auto-apply — every verdict becomes a confirmation and completion falls back to asking.
- Text applied from run results (verdict approvals, auto-apply, completion enforcement, and duplicated cards) now decodes HTML entities (`<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `&`, numeric forms) into their real symbols, so escaped model output no longer lands in card text.

- Bulk runs can now process more cards in parallel: the concurrency control goes up to the selected connection's parallel job limit (up to 16) instead of the previous fixed cap of 4. With the default connection chain, the limit of the connection marked default for agents is used.
- Completed results stay inspectable: applied and duplicated cards in a session now offer an **Inspect** action that opens their full diff view — the same review surface used for pending confirmations, read-only.

- Bulk runs can now enforce their successful outcomes when processing finishes: always apply in place, with cards edited mid-run held safely for review, or always duplicate using the session's configured name prefix or suffix.
- Completed and canceled sessions now offer **Run again**, creating a new queued session with the same configuration and targets while leaving the original run untouched.

- Completed runs whose cards were edited in place (confirm/auto save modes) now offer a **Duplicate applied cards** action in the session detail: one click creates a renamed clone per applied card, following the session's duplicate prefix/suffix naming. Cloned items stay marked Applied and show their copy.
- Group Chat's **Replace characters with generated cast** (Engine) now also includes characters whose run items were only applied in place — they are the run's output, so the replacement no longer silently drops them; items duplicated afterwards yield their clone instead.
- Requires Marinara Engine 2.4.8 (Capability API 1.68).

- Verdict review now always shows the full proposed field content below the colored diff when a field is expanded — no extra click needed. The expander button still reveals the complete colored diff and is relabeled "show all hunks →" accordingly.
- Requires Marinara Engine 2.4.8 (Capability API 1.68).

- The overlay workspace is interactive again: clicks, scrolling, and the close button reach the dialog instead of passing through to the chat underneath. Backdrop-click dismissal in the bulk dispatch dialog works again too.
- The workspace sizes to its content (up to min(92dvh, 60rem)) instead of forcing a 92dvh-tall dialog, so few or no sessions no longer leave a large empty void; long session lists scroll inside the dialog.
- Tidier workspace panes: consistent rail and detail padding, with the rail divider spanning the full workspace height.
- Requires Marinara Engine 2.4.8 (Capability API 1.68).

- The whole bulk flow now lives in an overlay workspace above the chat window (Capability API 1.68): session list, verdict review, diffs, and the dispatch dialog share one large two-pane surface instead of the cramped inline panel at the bottom of the agent settings.
- The sidebar selection action and the agent page open that workspace; engine controls can deep-link straight into a session or a prefilled dispatch through the `marinara:capability-overlay` event.
- The agent page keeps a compact status summary (active/past session counts) with an **Open Card Editor workspace** button.
- Requires Marinara Engine 2.4.8 (Capability API 1.68).

- When a character changes their status or activity during a call, the change now goes on their character card, as it does after a chat reply, so it shows in every chat and lasts for the time they gave. Before, the call changed only this chat's copy of their schedule, and the change was soon lost. (#1498)

- Opening a call no longer changes the volume of, or mutes, a reply Marinara is reading aloud in another chat. The call's voice volume and mute apply only to the call's own voices.
- A call in a chat that uses the Local Model now answers through Marinara's Local Model, as the chat does. Before, it stayed silent and showed no error.

- Calls now uses Marinara Engine's own settings, dialogs, voice playback, Local Model, Local Whisper, haptics, Spotify and chat saving instead of carrying copies of them. It no longer resets your Engine settings, starts a second Local Model, or overwrites chat changes saved while a call runs. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1478, #1487)
- During a call, the connection switcher and the sticker and emoji settings change the call's chat, not another chat.
- On phones, the Chat Settings bubble no longer covers the close button in Call Chat. It hides while Call Chat is open and comes back when you close it. (#1338)

- With a Claude (Subscription) connection, Calls no longer makes a hidden second request to name each session, and a request now stops with an error if Claude Code turns on claude.ai connectors. With a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0, Claude Code also no longer adds your account email, the date or this computer's details to the prompt. Engine 2.5.0's Claude Code still adds them, and the server log warns about it until you update Marinara. (#1313)
- Characters can call you on their own again. With the call command on, a character who decides to call you now rings with an incoming call. Before this, nothing happened.

- Mic recording calls no longer lose some of your speech with "Selected provider/model cannot receive provider-native audio input."
- A call left in a background tab or behind other windows no longer cuts a sentence into pieces at short pauses. It now waits until it has heard about 3 seconds of quiet, so replies there can take a little longer.

- Mic recording calls use your own speech-to-text server when it is turned on in Connections → Speech to Text (newer Engines). Local Whisper still handles speech when the server is off or fails.
- Speech you record while an earlier clip is still being transcribed now waits its turn instead of being dropped.
- Keep calls responsive when Safari blocks voice playback: wait for a new touch or key press, and let stopping a call cancel pending playback.
- SwarmUI video connections now generate character call clips using their saved workflow, resolution, frame rate, and LoRAs. Backup SwarmUI connections keep their own workflow settings.
- Keep required reasoning enabled for GLM 5.3 on NanoGPT and Z.AI when the selected effort is None.

- Includes upstream 1.11.0 to 1.13.0. Soldier, Elite and Boss enemy tiers; new chapters build toward a boss fight with contextual enemy dialogue. World-specific soundtrack briefs, stock and opt-in generated music and effects, and optional dialogue in assigned Engine character voices, with one mute control and channel volume sliders. Chapters and Character Stories play their own music cues. Fixes for legacy audio connections, achievement progress, small-choice autoplay, mobile playback, the Home layout and audio notices. Needs Capability API 1.381.

- Includes upstream 1.9.0 to 1.10.0. Choose your protagonist's dialogue or actions from two to four themed options; first-play choices become canon, and a chapter can end with one permanent big choice. Choices survive reloads and are on by default in Settings > Story > Continuity.
- An in-app fullscreen control beside Settings, and every Forge screen fills the available width and height. Needs Marinara Engine 2.5.1 and Capability API 1.376.
- Chapter controls, unit portraits and card icons are tidier.

- Includes upstream 1.8.14 and 1.8.15. On a phone turned sideways, world creation uses the whole screen width and scrolls as one page with a slim Back and Next row. Tapping a text field no longer zooms iPhone in. Ticking a cast member or outfit theme no longer scrolls the list back to the top on Safari-based browsers.
- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.

- Added Soldier, Elite and Boss enemy tiers in combat and enemy details.
- New story chapters build toward a boss confrontation using existing boss mechanics.
- Significant fights prepare contextual enemy dialogue, with local one-shot triggers and manual or Auto progression.
- Combat dialogue respects assigned character voices, mute and dialogue volume. Existing saved chapters and Tower encounters remain playable.

- Home shows a compact affinity matchup diagram beneath the communication button.
- Home backgrounds retain the top of the selected artwork below the game header.
- Combat shows one mute control without overlapping the other toolbar buttons.
- Autoplay resumes after a small story choice when it was enabled before the choice.
- Character communication keeps the composer visible when a mobile keyboard reduces the available height.

- Chapters and Character Stories generate and play their own music cues instead of reusing the Home track. Loading scenes keep the current track until their cue is ready.
- Small choices no longer block later shared narration or background pre-forging. Their alternatives remain generated together; playback, canon, replay and big-choice locks are preserved.
- Completion and compression still wait for pending selections to preserve canonical story history.
- Short audio notices no longer intercept taps on the game stage. Long reasons remain scrollable and stay visible while focused with a keyboard.
- Notice scrolling adapts when the panel becomes visible or changes size; replacing a long reason with short text restores dismissal.
- Recorded the actual merged Engine music-test baseline.

### New
- World-specific soundtrack briefs generated through the narration connection, cached for each music context and translated into original musical qualities.

### Fixed
- Audio failures show their HTTP status and, on newer Engine hosts, the provider's safe rejection reason while stock audio continues.
- Unit and relic achievements count every gained level; capped duplicates do not count as gained facets, and Tower-shop facet gains count.
- Existing worlds recover proven achievement progress without changing claimed rewards or pass progress.

- Fixed generated music and effects for worlds using migrated legacy audio connections.
- Recorded the merged Engine audio connection baseline.

### New
- Optional dialogue using explicitly assigned Engine character voices, with the current speech connection.
- Stock Game music and effects, plus opt-in generated audio reused per world and cue.
- A shared mute control, three precise channel volume sliders and configurable autoplay pacing.

### Fixed
- Home and story portrait frames include their bottom edge.

- New dialogue choices show intent labels instead of revealing the exact spoken line. Selected actions appear as narration; explicitly spoken choices remain protagonist dialogue.
- Existing untyped saved choices remain playable as narration. First-play canon, replay alternatives and permanent big decisions are preserved.
- Fixed: the Welcome Gift rewards no longer overlap Claim on short mobile screens. The event scrolls when needed, and Claim has a larger touch target.

- Choose your protagonist's dialogue or actions from two to four themed options above the dialogue box. Player choices are on by default in Settings > Story > Continuity.
- Small choices include every alternative scene in the same generation and return to the shared story. Your first-play choices become canon; replaying another route does not rewrite them.
- A chapter or Character Story can end with one optional big choice. That fate is permanent, and later story generation waits for it before continuing from the chosen outcome.
- Choices survive reloads. Existing linear chapters still work; turning choices off affects newly written scenes and keeps existing decisions.

- Chapter fullscreen controls now use a small icon aligned with the top-right header fade, with a usable touch target and visible keyboard focus.
- Visible unit portraits use eager loading and synchronous decoding on detail updates.
- Favorite and help icons are centered; unit cards show their existing affinity symbol in the top-right corner.

### New
- The fullscreen control beside Settings expands inside the Engine, hiding Home browser controls while keeping the Engine topbar. Outward/inward arrows show the action, and the button works on iPhone Safari too.
- Every Forge screen fills the available width and height instead of fitting a fixed 16:9 frame.
- A floating exit control stays available on screens without the shared toolbar and on the portrait rotation notice. Requires Engine capability API 1.376.

- Fixed: on iPhone and other Safari-based browsers, ticking a cast member or an outfit theme no longer scrolls the list (and, on a phone turned sideways, the whole world-creation page) back to the top.

- On a phone turned sideways, creating a world now uses the whole width of the screen and scrolls as one page: the title and the step tabs scroll away with the fields, and a slim Back and Next row stays at the bottom until you start typing.
- Fixed: tapping a text field in the game no longer makes iPhone zoom in.

- Fixed: places named in Korean, or in any other non-Latin script, get their background painted. Their names used to come out empty, so the background was never made; places whose names mixed Hangul and numbers could also share one background.
- Backgrounds already painted for a place keep showing; nothing is painted twice.
- On a phone held sideways the game uses more of the screen, text no longer grows when you turn the phone, and Settings packs its panels tighter. Where the browser has no fullscreen (iPhone Safari), the fullscreen button is hidden instead of doing nothing.

- Fixed: Character Stories can be merged too. In Settings > Continuity a compressed Character Story takes a tick like a chapter, and merges with the chapters next to it or with other Character Stories; the merged entry names each one, and the story never sends a merged one twice.
- Only chapters played to the end can be merged, and a merge that cannot happen says why.

- Fixed: a Tower boss that heals no longer gets back a quarter of its health with every Ultimate — it heals about as much as one of its escorts would, and the floor 40 boss is fitted to its floor again. In Water months, bosses no longer heal 8% of their health per Ultimate.
- Fixed: on a slow image connection, art is painted once: a chapter's backgrounds and enemies, banner art, portraits, key images, Bond backgrounds and outfits.
- Fixed: an outfit rotation keeps every outfit it already painted, even if the rest fails, and a Bond outfit you already have but that never counted as claimed is handed over instead of painted again.

- Includes upstream 1.4.87 to 1.4.90. The setup guide stays on the Memory Vault and shrinks to a bar elsewhere; the lexical-recall warning has a keyboard Reindex button and a failed status load offers Retry. Switching Long-Term Memory, recall settings and Reindex keep keyboard focus. The Memory Vault shows memories sooner, with rarer filters under Refine and one Edit selected sheet. Save confirms beside the button, the open memory is marked beyond colour, and the archive Undo banner keeps its count.

- Includes upstream 1.4.86. Keyboard focus moves somewhere sensible after each action, and field errors sit under their fields. Results show beside the action that made them. The layout follows the width of its own panel, batch bars stay in view, and small controls are easier to tap. Long lists stay responsive. Warning notices show an icon and a stronger border.

- Includes upstream 1.4.85: keyboard and focus fixes. Sources rows are reachable with Tab and open with Enter or Space. Accepting a Review Queue change keeps the list and your place while memories reload. Memory Vault dialogs show on a narrow panel. Place picker arrow keys keep the highlight in view. Backup controls have a cleaner Tab order and screen-reader name.

- Includes upstream 1.4.58 to 1.4.84. Other Agents can ask for memories about the characters they write as, and packages can no longer reach the memory vault itself, only memories a character has everywhere.
- New "Finish cut-off answers" setting asks the model for the rest of an extraction answer cut at the output limit.
- Many reliability fixes: names starting with "Char" or "Rel", digit-led ids, shared-memory review instead of private copies, one background recall-index rebuild, a capped Memory Vault list, a 1.5 MB debug-log trim, and no raw error text (file paths) in messages.
- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.
- The Undo banner after archiving keeps saying how many memories it will restore, even when you save another memory while it is showing.

- The Memory Vault shows your memories sooner: rarer filters sit under Refine and open by themselves while in use, and changing several memories happens in one Edit selected sheet, with Archive and Delete kept apart.
- Changing availability for several memories now says how many will change, stay the same or be blocked, explains why Apply is off, and repeats Apply under the list.
- Saving a memory now confirms beside the Save button, and a save that waits on a recall rebuild says so as a warning instead of an error.
- The memory you have open is now marked with an edge bar and announced to screen readers, not only by a tint.
- The memory info panel now has one name everywhere you open it.

- Switching Long-Term Memory on or off, changing a chat's recall settings and running Reindex no longer drop keyboard focus while they work.
- The unsaved-changes prompt now says where you are going, and the Chat Settings panel is shorter, names the right button and no longer shows made-up defaults while loading.

- The setup guide now stays on the Memory Vault and shrinks to a one-line bar elsewhere, steps out of the way when one of its buttons takes you to another screen, and lets you choose Not now, Don't show again or Done. Later steps follow the source type you picked.
- The lexical-recall warning now has its own Reindex button you can reach by keyboard, and a failed status load offers Retry instead of a dead end.

- Keyboard focus now moves somewhere sensible after you act in Review, the Memory Vault, Sources, the setup guide, Settings and Debug, and field errors sit under their fields and are read with them.
- Results show beside the action that made them. Sources names a failed or partial import as such, and Review and Sources say why Accept or Import is off.
- Long-Term Memory lays out by the width of its own panel, so a narrow side panel gets the phone layout. Batch bars stay in view while you scroll, and checkboxes, toggles, links and info buttons are easier to tap.
- Long lists stay responsive: Sources searches once you pause typing and keeps the current rows meanwhile, and place pickers show 100 places at a time with a Show more row.
- Warning notices show a warning icon and a stronger border instead of relying on color, and error notices show their border and have room inside.

- Five keyboard and focus fixes. In Sources, Tab now reaches the name of each chat or character source in the list, and Enter or Space opens it, so Re-extract, Manage, Review and Open memory work without a mouse. Accepting a change in the Review Queue no longer hides the queue while the memories it shows reload: the list, your place in it and the keyboard position stay, a small spinner shows beside "Review Queue", and Accept waits until the memories have reloaded. On a narrow panel, the Memory Vault's "Rename details" and unsaved-changes dialogs now show instead of leaving the screen frozen. Arrow keys in the place picker keep the highlighted place in view. In Memory Settings, Tab after "Choose backup" goes straight to "Reset settings", and screen readers name "Choose backup" once.

- Other Agents can now ask Long-Term Memory for memories about the characters they write as, ranked against what they are about to write. They get only memories available to that character everywhere: never memories limited to a chat or group, archived memories or suggestions, and they can't change anything. A new setting in Memory Settings, "Other Agents can read memories" (on by default), turns this off, also for Slurp's "What your other Agents know", and names the Agents that read memories lately. Each read shows in Activity as "Read by another Agent".

- Other installed Agents can no longer reach the memory vault itself. The storage service Long-Term Memory shares with other packages now offers one read, the memories available to a character everywhere, which is what Slurp's flavour brief uses. Memories limited to a chat or group, imported sources, archived and game-only memories, suggestions and the vault folder stay private.

- Once the debug log reaches its 2 MB limit, Long-Term Memory now trims it to the newest 1.5 MB instead of to just under 2 MB. Before, every new debug line rewrote the whole file from then on, and saves and recalls waited for each rewrite. Now the lines after a trim are added to the end of the file again. The log keeps between 1.5 and 2 MB of the newest lines.

- Memory Settings has a new setting beside "Maximum output tokens", "Finish cut-off answers", off by default. With it on, when the model's extraction answer stops at the output limit, Long-Term Memory asks the model for the rest, with up to 3 extra requests for that source, each sending the source again. With it off, a source cut off this way now says that Retry will stop at the same place and names the setting.
- No change in what Long-Term Memory does. Internally, the server file that matches names in chats and summaries to memories is split into four files.

- Extraction from a structured chat summary now reads a character name that starts with "Char", such as "Char Aznable", or a relationship pair whose first name starts with "Rel", as a name instead of an id when the summary writes the name out, as in "- Char Aznable | …", "character: Char Aznable", "- Rel Varga, Sayla Mass | …" or "characters: Rel Varga, Sayla Mass". The section the summary gives that character, such as Profile, now reaches their memory, those lines are saved instead of being dropped as not in the chat's roster, and a relationship that only the summary mentions is kept. The event made for a relationship's cause names the pair as the summary wrote it, as in "Rel Varga and Sayla Mass relationship changed after the hangar fire.", instead of splitting the names into words. A line that writes an id made from the name instead, such as "subject: char_aznable", is still read as an id.

- Two more places no longer show raw error text, which could include file paths. In the integrity list in memory settings, a note file or event log that cannot be read now says "Note file vault/… could not be read or validated." or "Event log could not be read.", followed by "Details are in the server log."; a note whose contents are broken still says what is wrong with it. When importing or re-extracting a source fails because the memory model or its settings could not be loaded for a server reason, Sources and Review show their usual "could not be imported" or "could not be re-extracted" message and the error goes to the server log. Messages that tell you how to fix the model setup, such as "Choose a language model connection before generating content.", show as before.

- Extraction now saves facts about a character whose name starts with "Char", such as "Char Aznable", or a relationship whose first name starts with "Rel", to the memory chosen for them instead of a second memory under a shorter id, and no longer drops events about them as linked to a missing memory. The same holds for any chosen memory whose id repeats its prefix, such as an imported char_char_mara. A memory already saved under the shorter id keeps receiving facts only while it is linked to the character or titled with its full name; if you have two memories for one character, merge them in the app.

- A few more unexpected failures no longer show their raw error text, which could include file paths. In Sources, a source that could not be saved or extracted now says "Failed to write imported source note." or "Failed to extract imported source.", followed by "Details are in the server log."; this includes the model provider rejecting the request during an import. In Review, a change that could not be checked says "Long-term memory preflight failed. Details are in the server log." An identity repair in settings whose backup could not be restored says so without the cause. The full error is written to the server log. Messages written for you, such as a model reply that was cut off, show as before.

Memory Nag now uses Marinara Engine's own libraries and data cache for its screens instead of carrying copies of them, so the download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1487)

Scans now read Roleplay whispers the way the Engine's own agents do, marked private with who they were for, so a promise made in a whisper can become a memory. A message that is only a whisper is no longer read as empty. This needs a Marinara Engine that shares whispers with Agents; older versions keep reading public messages only.
The description now says what it does in plain words.

Automatic scans wait while a manual message-range scan is active, avoiding duplicate model charges between batches. Finished, stopped, failed, and abandoned scans release the guard without losing checkpoint progress.
Send the saved admin secret on plain-HTTP remote clients too, matching the Engine, so Create Memories no longer fails with an X-Admin-Secret error on LAN and Termux setups.

Choose all unprocessed messages or a specific message range when creating vault memories, so long chats can skip stale history. Closing the progress or prompt window keeps the underlying chat settings open.

- Includes upstream 1.5.8 and 1.5.9: image failures the Engine marks nonretryable no longer start automatic replacement requests, and the sticker, emoji, picture and poll menus open inside Noodle and are no longer see-through.
- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.
- Image failures marked nonretryable by the Engine no longer start automatic replacement requests.
- The sticker, emoji, picture and poll menus now open inside Noodle. That hides the chat emoji-selection settings, which 1.5.7 meant to hide but still showed, and the menus are no longer see-through.

- Noodle now uses Marinara Engine's own settings, dialogs, notifications, Local Model and connection queue instead of carrying copies of them. It no longer resets your Engine settings or starts a second Local Model, its background refreshes wait while a chat on the same connection is replying, and its notifications appear where you put yours. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1478, #1487)
- The sticker and emoji pickers no longer show the chat emoji-selection settings. Those belong to a chat, and Noodle has none.

- With a Claude (Subscription) connection, Noodle no longer makes a hidden second request to name each session, and a request now stops with an error if Claude Code turns on claude.ai connectors. With a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0, Claude Code also no longer adds your account email, the date or this computer's details to the prompt. Engine 2.5.0's Claude Code still adds them, and the server log warns about it until you update Marinara. (#1313)

- Each character can now use their own image generation connection for Noodle images. Open the character's Noodle profile, choose Edit profile and pick it under Image connection. The choice saves right away. Use Noodle image connection keeps the connection from Noodle's settings. Noodle still needs an image connection in its settings or a default image connection before it makes images.

- The switch that adds a character's image instructions to their Noodle images is now in Noodle. Open the character's Noodle profile, choose Edit profile and find it under the profile fields. Edit image instructions opens the character's Convo tab, where you write the instructions. Your current choice carries over. The link needs Marinara Engine with capability API 1.67; on an older Engine, the switch works without the link.

- Interpret image prompts now works without an Agents default connection. When none is set under Settings → Connections → Defaults, Noodle's own text connection rewrites the image prompt. Before, the rewrite was skipped, so your image connection's Image Prompting Instructions had no effect and the style profile's Style text was pasted into the prompt.
- Include descriptions now gives the character's appearance notes to the AI that rewrites the image prompt instead of leaving them in the prompt it edits, where they reached ComfyUI as plain text. With Interpret image prompts off, the notes are still added as written.
- Style text you write into Auto or a copy of it now guides the rewrite too.
- If the rewrite copies a full sentence of your Image Prompting Instructions, the Style text or the character's image habits, Noodle removes it. Short phrases and tag lists such as "masterpiece, best quality" stay.
- The help texts now say what happens when Interpret image prompts is off.

- Image prompts no longer include text meant for the AI that writes them. The poster's Personality and image habits and your image connection's Image Prompting Instructions now only guide the rewrite that Interpret image prompts runs. Before, Noodle pasted them word for word into the prompt sent to ComfyUI and other image services, which broke tag-only prompts. With Interpret image prompts off, or when the rewrite fails, the image service gets the prompt without them.
- A style profile's Style text now reaches the rewrite once, as guidance, instead of also sitting in the prompt it edits. The Auto profile's note "Infer a consistent visual style from the character, game, scene, and selected image model" never ends up in the image prompt. Style text from the other profiles still applies when no rewrite runs.

- New Show images to the writer switch in Settings → Advanced → Image Understanding. Turn it off and Noodle never sends timeline images to the model that writes your timeline. Image captioning, when on, still sends them to the captioning connection, which is the Noodle generation connection unless you choose another. The switch is on by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it off.
- The Image captioning help now says what happens when it is off: the writer model gets up to 8 recent timeline images, if Show images to the writer is on and the model accepts them.

- Noodle can now translate posts and comments for you. Turn on Translate posts automatically in Settings → General. It uses the translator defaults you saved in a chat's Translation settings and leaves what your personas wrote alone. Posts already in your language get no extra copy, and turning the switch off stops the translations still waiting.
- Translations now stay after you refresh the timeline, leave Noodle or reload the page, and a translation you hide stays hidden. This browser keeps them, so another device translates again.

- Fixed timeline refreshes on local models that failed after a short, empty-looking answer. When the prompt plus the room Noodle keeps for its answer did not fit the connection's context window, Noodle cut your characters, chats and timeline out of the prompt before sending. It now keeps the whole prompt and lowers the answer limit instead. If too little room is left for an answer, the refresh stops and says what to turn down.

- You can now translate posts and comments, your own included. Pick Translate in a post's menu or under a comment, and use the same button to hide it again. Noodle uses the translator defaults you saved in a chat's Translation settings, or Google Translate into English if you have not saved any.
- In Chrome on Android, adding a picture to a post or comment now offers the camera as well as your files. The Marinara Android app doesn't offer the camera yet.
- Noodle's description now says what it is in plain words.
- When Noodle cannot load, it now says so instead of showing an empty timeline. If Marinara Engine blocked it because this device has no Admin Secret, it explains how to set one.
- Widgets on Homescreen now available.
- Search icons and post menus keep Noodle's selected accent when Engine Chroma animates.

- Applying a saved prompt asks before replacing the current prompt, including edits already saved as the active prompt.
- Cancel works immediately in Delete All Noodle Data; only deletion requires typing DELETE.
- A running timeline refresh blocks duplicate refresh requests instead of queuing extra generations.
- GLM 5.3 on NanoGPT and Z.AI keeps its required reasoning enabled when the selected effort is None.
- Maintenance: simplify the inline composer's visibility checks and remove unused code.

- Fixed a manually chosen profile avatar being replaced by the character card image.
- Applying a saved prompt now asks before it discards unsaved prompt changes.
- Ambient accounts no longer post images.
- Removed leftover NoodleR wording from the image generation settings.

- Includes upstream 0.7.2. Korean, Japanese and Chinese names now count when followed directly by a particle or written without spaces, so Update from History, automatic updates and Scene-only recognise them. A longer card name no longer counts as a shorter one, and a rejected persona perception names the name it expected.

- On phones, the Relationship Tracker icon in the chat's tracker strip no longer shows as a button that does nothing. The relationship web now opens from its own tracker window, which you can move like the other phone trackers (needs a matching Marinara Engine update).
- Version renumbered to 10.0.1 so every package follows one fork-wide line. No behavior change.

- Korean, Japanese and Chinese now work. A name followed directly by a Korean particle (김민수는) or written without spaces in Japanese (アリスは) or Chinese (张三很信任李四) now counts as naming that character. Before, Update from History and automatic updates rejected these sentences, and Scene-only couldn't tell who was present.
- A longer card name doesn't count as a shorter one: 김민수 isn't 김민, and アリス isn't リス. Single characters and syllables appear inside ordinary words, so a one-character Chinese or Japanese name still needs a space or punctuation next to it, and a one-syllable Korean name counts only before a particle (준은, but not 준비).
- When a persona perception is rejected, the message now says which name it expected.

- When Update from History can't use the model's answer, it now shows the changes the model suggested instead of only an error. Each change uses character names, says in plain words what needs fixing, and can be edited, removed or saved. Relationship changes and persona perceptions are saved separately, and the model's original answer is under Details for bug reports.
- Fewer "unknown character alias" errors: the tracker now tells the model to keep your persona out of character pairs, and a pair it still files with your persona is offered as that character's view of you. The error now names the alias the model used.
- Update from History no longer fails when the model leaves out an empty list.
- After saving only persona perceptions, the panel says how many it saved.

- In Roleplay, Update from History now reads whispers the way the Engine's own agents do, marked private with who they were for. A message that is only a whisper is no longer read as empty.
- This needs a Marinara Engine that shares whispers with Agents. On older versions, the tracker keeps reading public messages only.

- Fixed Update from History failing with "Persona update 1 must contain exactly five values" when a persona is active. The tracker now tells the model the exact shape of a persona perception, so it stops copying the lock flag into its answer.
- The same fix helps automatic updates, which were quietly skipping those persona perception changes.
- If a model still returns the wrong shape, the error now says how many values it sent.

- In the Tracker Panel, Relationship Tracker now has the same collapsible header as World, Persona and the other trackers instead of its own card, and remembers whether you collapsed it. While it runs, the header shows a small spinner.
- In the desktop Trackers window, the drawer's own header is used, and Relationship Tracker's button now matches the other trackers' buttons.

- Fixed "Invalid or missing X-Admin-Secret header" when Marinara is opened from another device (LAN, phone, or proxy). The panel now sends the admin secret saved on that device and explains where to save it.
- Update from History falls back to the default agent connection, then the chat's, when no tracker connection is chosen.
- Automatic runs keep valid changes when the model omits an empty list or returns one malformed persona entry.
- Switching persona or removing a card mid-run no longer reports a failed run.
- Tapping a line label or finishing an automatic update no longer wipes unsaved editor text or closes open sections.
- The persona no longer covers a lone character or sits under relationship lines, and its arrowheads show.
- The lock checkbox stays beside its label at Compact width; status colours are readable in the light theme.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.

- Two prompt-injection modes: All relationships, or Scene-only relationships. Presence lookback (default 15 messages) decides Scene-only eligibility; the automatic tracker's Context Size (default 5) is separate.
- Touch and pen: press a relationship line to reveal its label and press elsewhere to dismiss it; desktop keeps hover and keyboard-focus labels.
- Read-only API for other packages: GET /api/relationship-tracker/v1/chats/:chatId/relationships.

One release for everything built since 0.3.53 (unreleased 0.3.54 to 0.3.65 folded in):

- Storylines: arcs, dramas and situations run on one storyline engine; Story Packs import v2 files, one JSON `fit`, one Packs list with a gate and Remove, topic switches `<pack>:<topic>`.
- Packs (off by default): Family pack and five kink packs (Lingerie, Cosplay, Feet, Dom/sub, Exhibition).
- Intimacy ladder: rapport tiers open doors in DMs (`slurpRapportDoors`), the highest tier is kept.
- Paid sexting sessions (`SlpSextingBar`); Stir as a slide-up sheet (`SlpStirDeck`); Stories in Slurp's own layer.
- Fixes: DM prompts know the player's latest public posts, @tagged Creators join the picture cast, tag-list looks go over whole, picture prompt rewrite floor 8192, wardrobe tag commas, neutral wording; Images > Advanced "Keep original picture files".

- Image failures marked nonretryable by the Engine no longer start automatic replacement requests. Slurp also stops later background retries for posts and Creator artwork, and keeps post prompts for a deliberate retry.

- Fixed: an automatic post no longer reads a Creator's card or refreshes shared ideas with the AI while one of your chats on the same connection is replying, and an automatic post no longer makes your other automatic work (Noodle's too) wait 30 seconds. A new Creator's first automatic post no longer refuses itself.
- Fixed: Write, Improve, Draft voice, Generate schedule, the page style and "Let <Creator> design it", a plan you ask for, an appearance you generate and picture descriptions for replies now take their turn on your connection like your chats, so automatic work waits for them.

- Changed: Slurp now uses Marinara Engine's own settings, dialogs, notifications, Local Model and connection queue instead of carrying copies of them. It no longer resets your Engine settings or starts a second Local Model, its background work waits while a chat on the same connection is replying, and its notifications appear where you put yours. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1478, #1487)
- Changed: the sticker and emoji pickers no longer show the chat emoji-selection settings. Those belong to a chat, and Slurp has none.

- Added: tapping an ad (the button, the picture or a wall tile) opens an ad sheet with the picture, brand, product, copy and price feel, and still records the tap. The old "Opening … promotion" toast is gone.
- Added: Settings › Fans & money › Collect has a "Daily limit on Collect" switch (`walletPayoutDailyLimit`, on by default). Off, Collect moves every whole coin of your Creator earnings at once.
- Added: Messaging › "What fans ask for" is an editable list for the wish in a commission request (`messagesCommissionAsks`); empty keeps the built-in asks.

- Fixed: restoring a backup checks each media file more closely. Only PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF and AVIF pictures whose file extension matches their contents come back; anything else is skipped and listed with the skipped entries (#1476).
- Fixed: AVIF pictures in a backup were dropped on restore. They now come back like the other formats.
- Changed: Slurp sends every stored picture (posts, messages, avatars, banners, ads) as the image type its contents show (#1476).

- Changed: Creators whose character has a Conversation Schedule now follow it. Slurp only read a bare "06:00" and the Engine stores ranges ("06:00-08:00"), so every block was dropped and availability was guessed from the last post. Ranges, including ones past midnight, are now read as the Engine reads them. Time between blocks is free time, online; a block's status decides (offline and dnd are away, online and idle answer); a block without one falls back to its activity words. The post brief's day plan reads the same ranges (#1436).
- Fixed: a promised follow-up could be postponed forever while the Creator read as away. More than 12 hours past its first due time, it now goes out at its next check even if they are away. A fan waiting for a reply, a cool-off and night quiet still hold it (#1436).
- Fixed: a name only matches inside one tag or line ("summer, rain" is not "Summer Rain"), and companion reference pictures come only from the companions found in the scene.

- Fixed: in tag mode, a Creator's identity tags ("Always in their pictures" or the card name) stayed where the prompt writer put them, often behind the count and body tags. Whole tags now move to the front of the Creator's part, once, in the writer's spelling (#1428).
- Fixed: "The image model knows this character" added the card name a second time when the writer used tag order ("ryuuzaki umi" for "Umi Ryuuzaki"). Names now match in any word order.
- Fixed: a companion the writer named by their card or tag name got no look, no reference picture, and kept the one-person rule. Companions now match on display or card name, whole words in any order (#1429).

- Added: Creators react to each other. Each hour a character Creator may like or comment on another Creator's public post (about two a day), persona Creators' posts included. Free canned copy; no messages, tips or subscriptions between Creators.
- Fixed: the browsing persona was saved per browser, so one install could show an empty Inbox on one device and 87 unread on another. The pick is now a Slurp setting shared by every device; an older per-browser pick is saved once.
- Fixed: the custom tag field greyed out with no reason when a draft had filled all eight tags. It now says so.
- Fixed: Hinted profiles checked tags joined with the bio, so words from separate fields could add up to a copied source detail. Tags are checked one at a time, and the save error names the tag that leaks.

- Fixed: picture prompts carried the style profile's tags twice. The prompt writer now gets the bare draft; the style is compiled onto its result once.
- Fixed: the gallery fallback picked the first gallery image every time. It now picks the image this Creator showed least recently.
- Added: "Draw missing avatars and banners" in Settings › Images. Off stops background drawing; Open Creators still copy their card's pictures. On for existing installs; first-run setup sets it from its images choice.
- Added: "Caption instructions" in Settings › Images. Blank uses a Slurp default that describes people, clothes, pose, place and text, and leaves out the art style.
- Added: "Always in their pictures" per Creator. The text opens the Creator's part of every picture prompt, after the style tags, in place of the card name.
- Fixed: the post writer no longer dresses Creators in worn-out, faded or shabby clothes unless the card or caption asks for it.

- Added: trends. A post that takes off (shown likes; your likes, unlocks and tips count most), your own page's hits, a platform trend, or Stir "Start a trend" (ready-made trends, a starter, what to lean into) starts one. Stir "Steer a trend" changes what it leans into. The right Creators join, each at their own spice level and limits, quote the origin post, peak, then cool; some roast it, some never join. The starter gains followers.
- Added: Discover "Trending on Slurp" row, a trend chip on posts, and trend search.
- Changed: the invented "silly trend" daily-life moment is gone; trend posts skip the feed spice damping.

- Fixed: long DMs end at a sentence or word (up to 2400 characters), and commission quotes use the Creator's own prices.
- Fixed: Cancel ends a subscription to a removed Creator at once.
- Fixed: fans react to what a picture shows, not its art style.
- Fixed: post drift. Tips no longer teach a guessed taste, and a spicy kind or taste that other Creators posted that day steps aside, so the whole feed is not in the shower at once. Spice level is unchanged.
- Changed: family is never paired up on its own. Cards that say they are lovers, or the player in Stir, still can.
- Fixed: clearer "monogamous" message in Stir, with the Relationships switch on the Creator sheet.
- Fixed: work mode no longer blurs the coin and G's face; Couples pages are not a missing source; the sign-up scene names an unreachable connection.
- Fixed: a scheduled post goes up once, and a shared-page post waits its turn.

- Added: chats with "Carryover to chats" on also learn the character's Slurp storyline, love life, how well they know you, and the Slurp memories a chat with you may read.
- Added: Carryover settings show in how many chats with your Creators "Include Slurp activity" is on.
- Fixed: a scene started from a DM runs on the connection Slurp planned it with, not the Engine's plain default.
- Fixed: an unreadable scene plan is asked for once more before "The scene plan got lost" shows.
- Fixed: "Start the scene" shows an error when the Engine's scene host is missing.
- Fixed: lorebook entries set to "At Depth" reach Slurp DMs and posts.
- Added: Deep details has a "Lore" section with the entries a reply used or had no room for.

- Faster: Slurp shows character and persona avatars as small copies instead of the full card picture. On opening Slurp the feed downloaded about 16 MB of avatar pictures (1–2.5 MB each, shown 44 px wide), and Discover about 14 MB more; those downloads also held up the feed's other requests. The small copies are made once and kept in Slurp's own media folder.
- Faster: the "Report" sheet of a post or a reply is built only when you open it. Before, every post card and reply built a closed copy, which made the feed and Creator pages slower to open.
- Faster: the ambient background colour measures the pictures on screen only after the screen has drawn, so opening a screen no longer forces extra layout work.

- Changed: Slurp follows a Creator's gender instead of calling everyone "she". Drama packs use the gender of whoever plays each role ("{her:he}" tokens), and pack names and descriptions no longer assume a woman. Post, DM and scene prompts tell the model the Creator's pronouns. A Creator without a gender is "they".
- Added: a "Clothing style" choice in the Creator's stage profile: Auto, Feminine, Masculine or Neutral. Auto follows gender. It decides what a "lingerie" spice post is: lingerie for feminine, an underwear shoot with briefs for masculine, either for neutral. Male Creators no longer get bra-and-panties shoots unless their style is Feminine. The post prompt also names the style.
- Added: a picture of a Creator whose appearance text does not say their sex starts with "Male." or "Female." from their gender, so the image model stops defaulting to a woman.
- Changed: the stage profile field hints read "he", "she" or "they" from the gender you picked.

- Fixed: on Android, choosing a picture for a post (in the composer, or "replace" while editing a post) no longer opens the system photo picker, which lists only a few albums such as Camera, Screenshots and Downloads. Android now offers its full file browser, so every folder is reachable. A file that is not a picture still gets "Choose an image file.". Other platforms keep the picture-only file dialog. (#1378)

- Added: in a Creator's settings, "Appearance for pictures" has a new button, "Use the card's image tags". It shows only while the linked character or persona has the Image Appearance Override switched on and filled in, and it saves those tags as the Creator's own appearance. It asks first when that replaces an appearance you wrote. "Use linked appearance" (or "Clear override") removes it again. (#1366)
